events.text: {npc} tries to rise and cannot. {He} spits to one side and looks up at you without asking for anything. {He} would not take it from you even if you offered.

events.text: The fight is over and {npc} is still breathing hard on the ground between you. A crowd has gathered at a polite distance. Somebody in it says, quite clearly, "Finish it."

choices.text: By the old rules: the loser walks

effects.log: You nod once and leave {him} the wall.

choices.text: By your rules: the loser limps

effects.log: You decide the old rules are too kind.

choices.text: By the hardest rule: the loser never fights again

effects.log: You decide the old rules are not kind enough.

events.text: Rain on the stones, and {npc} face down in it. {He} turns {his} head to look at you. "Well?" {he} says. "I would not have stopped."

effects.log: You leave {him} in the rain.
You make sure of it.

choices.text: Make sure {he} is never a danger again

effects.log: Two fingers, and the rain goes on falling.

events.text: {npc} is waiting at the crossroads as if you had an appointment. {He} is stronger than when you last met; you can see it in how {he} stands. "I have thought about you every day," {he} says. "Every single day."

effects.log: It takes the whole evening and most of a jar. At the end of it {he} only looks tired, and goes home.
{He} lets you go. You hear {him} laugh behind you for a long way.

events.text: A letter under your door, in a hand you know: "The old place, at the new moon. Come alone, or I will come to you." It is signed {npc}.

effects.log: You talk at the old place until the moon is down. {npc} leaves without drawing, which is the most {he} has ever given you.
You burn it. A week later you hear {npc} told the whole teahouse you did not come.

events.text: {npc} walks into the inn where you are eating and sits down across from you without asking. There is a new scar on {his} hand and a new calm in {his} eyes, which is worse. "Finish your soup," {he} says. "Then we go outside."

effects.log: {He} wants to be seen. You see {him}, for an hour, and it turns out to be enough.
The cook does not even look up. Behind you, {npc} starts on your soup.

events.text: People on the road are talking about {npc}: a string of fights won since you last met, and every one of them, {he} tells anyone who listens, practice for you.

events.text: {npc} comes to find you with two juniors at {his} back. {He} is a senior of the house whose young one you broke, and {he} is not here to talk about it. "You know why I have come," {he} says.

ok.log: {npc} goes down in front of the people {he} brought to watch. {He} leaves without a word, and you know this is not over.

fail.log: {npc} puts you on the ground without hurrying. "That is all," {he} says. "We are even now." And for that house, it seems, you are.

effects.log: You pay, and you bow, and it costs you more than the silver. {npc} takes both and goes.

choices.text: Bow low and ask the house's pardon

effects.log: You bow until your forehead is a hand from the floor. {npc} lets you stay there a long time before {he} leaves.

events.text: Word reaches you before {npc} does: the house is sending someone. Then {he} is at your door, a senior of that house with old calluses and no patience. "Outside," {he} says.

effects.log: The silver arrives before you have finished talking. {npc} weighs it in one hand and nods.

choices.text: Shut the door and wait for {him} to leave

effects.log: {He} leaves after a day and a night. Everyone in the street saw {him} wait, and saw you not come out.

events.text: {npc} stands in the middle of the market road where everyone can see, and calls your name, and the name of the one you hurt. A senior of that house does not send letters.

effects.log: The go-between is very good and very expensive, and by evening it is done.

choices.text: Leave the town by the back road

effects.log: You leave by the back road. The market road remembers.

events.text: {npc} is old, and walks slowly, and every fighter on the road steps aside for {him} without being asked. {He} is the master of the one you beat at your door. "Twice," {he} says. "I will not need a third time."

effects.log: You kneel in the road. {npc} lets you kneel until the sun moves, and then {he} walks away.

events.text: The house has stopped sending its seniors. This time {npc} came, the master of them all, and sat down in your courtyard to wait for you like a guest. "Sit," {he} says. "Then stand, and we will see."

effects.log: You say it plainly. {npc} hears you out, and leaves without a word, and the whole road knows you said it.

events.text: {npc} stops you on the road with an open hand, and looks at your face for a long time. "You stand like your master stands," {he} says. "Your master shamed me once, before everyone I knew. I cannot reach your master. I can reach you."

fail.log: {npc} stands over you a while. "Tell your master I was here," {he} says, and goes.

choices.text: Ask {him} what happened, all of it

effects.log: It is a long story and an old one, and by the end of it {he} is tired of carrying it. You carry it a little way for {him}.
{He} watches you go. You have the feeling you will see {him} again.

events.text: A stranger blocks the door of the teahouse: {npc}, grey at the temples, with a grudge older than you are. "I knew your master," {he} says, "when your master was young and cruel. I have been waiting a long time for someone who carries that name."

fail.log: {npc} leaves you among the tea bowls. "Better," {he} says, "than I hoped. Not good enough."

effects.log: You hear it. It does not make your master look good. {npc} finishes the cup and goes, lighter than {he} came.
{He} lets you pass. You hear {him} ask the owner which way you live.

events.text: {npc} has come a long way to find you, and says so. "Your master took something from me that I cannot take back," {he} says. "So I will take something from what your master made."

effects.log: "They are now," {he} says, and leaves you to think about that.

events.text: Since the day your dantian broke, the energy will not gather; you sit to breathe and nothing comes. Then a pedlar of medicines tells you about a healer in the far hills who has mended worse. Maybe. Once.

effects.log: You set out with what you have. It is a long road, and you are slower on it than you used to be.
You let the name go by. It will come round again.

events.text: An old monk who sweeps the steps of a mountain temple watches you climb them and says, without being asked, "Broken at the centre. I know someone who mends that."

effects.log: The monk gives you a name and a direction, and goes back to sweeping.

choices.text: Thank the monk and go on

effects.log: You thank the monk. The name stays with you all the same.

events.text: The healer is real, and tiny, and very rude. You can be mended, the healer says, but the price is not silver: a year of carrying water and grinding roots, and a herb from the cliff that nobody young will climb for.

choices.text: Carry the water for a year

effects.log: A year of buckets and roots and silence. At the end of it the healer looks at you differently.

choices.text: Pay for the herb to be brought instead

effects.log: A climber brings the herb down, and the healer grumbles that it is cheating, and takes it.
You go back down the hill. The healer does not watch you go.

events.text: The healer listens to your pulse for an hour and says it can be done, but slowly, and not cheaply: rare roots, a season of needles, and patience you do not have yet.

choices.text: Stay the season and learn patience

effects.log: A season of needles and bitter tea. You learn a little patience, which surprises both of you.

choices.text: Pay for the rarest roots in the province

effects.log: The roots cost a great deal. The healer says they are worth it, and does not smile.
You go. The pulse the healer felt goes with you.

events.text: Everything is ready: the roots, the needles, the cold room. The healer warns you plainly. The mending hurts more than the breaking did, and some people stop it halfway.

effects.log: Three days and three nights. You do not stop it.
The healer shrugs and covers the needles. They will be ready when you are.

events.text: The last step is the hardest, the healer says: the broken well is opened again with your own qi, and you will have to find that qi in the dark, where it went.

choices.text: Go into the dark and find it

effects.log: You find it, far down, a thread of warmth. You follow it back.
The healer gives you time, as if it were a small thing.
